analysis: The only change in this PR is a documentation addition to docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines ~1561-1569). It describes how LocalTokenizerBridge.decode releases trailing <0xHH> byte-fallback tokens, so Gemma 4 text with characters outside its vocabulary is no longer dropped. DetokenizerV2 holds back partial runs shown as U+FFFD. The supplied base text units (lines 3235-4002) are unchanged context: Flint constraints, cluster placement, link and share probes, and tensor-parallel kernels. The patch touches no code, so no trust boundary, key, attestation, authorization, prefix-cache (T-041) or encryption behavior changes. The described tokenizer fix is output-correctness behavior inside the provider process. It does not touch the coordinator wire contract (TB-002) or plaintext handling (T-008), and the doc claims no new file or network exposure. The behavior it documents (LocalTokenizerLoader.swift) is not in the supplied evidence, so the code's correctness and any security impact, such as an unbounded buffer for a run of byte tokens, were not verified. This is a coverage limit, not a finding. The cluster, probe-history and share-probe sections in the base context mention owner-only files under ~/.darkbloom/cluster. I treated them as pre-existing and unchanged. I identified no security regression and no threat-model gap from this PR.
